source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 9 (2022), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.209
title: Exact heat-shape desensitization when the control contains the observation boundary
difficulty_reason: Design nested cutoffs in the coupled forward/backward equations and their commutator corrections so that the adjoint vanishes outside the observation region while the resulting control remains supported in the boundary collar. This is a constructive PDE localization argument, not a direct implication of approximate controllability.

context_spans.label: standard shape derivative and coupled forward-backward system

standard_prerequisites.name: Classical heat equation and functional analysis
standard_prerequisites.statement: Weak and transposition solutions, Sobolev trace maps and parabolic regularity, Holmgren unique continuation, Hilbert-space range/kernel duality, standard heat observability and convex minimization. The displayed Hadamard derivative formula is a standard supplied input. Target-specific constructions remain in the original proof.

core_obligations: Design nested cutoffs in the coupled forward/backward equations and their commutator corrections so that the adjoint vanishes outside the observation region while the resulting control remains supported in the boundary collar. This is a constructive PDE localization argument, not a direct implication of approximate controllability.

compared.difference: Public 2109 is finite-dimensional exactness plus global approximation in disjoint geometry. The present target is all-direction exactness in a boundary-collar geometry, obtained by a separate cutoff/commutator construction; the interior-observation easy case is not counted.

dedup.scope: Compared same-source public manifest item, existing heat obstruction card and the three new heat targets; no direct desensitization corollaries counted.
